issue.title: [Bug] Under pandas 3, generated wrangling code coerces string columns to numeric, empties bike_model/date, and reports every row as invalid, missing or duplicated
issue.body:
## Description

Under pandas 3, the agent's generated wrangling code sometimes wipes out the dataset's text columns and then reports the result as a data-quality finding. The generated functions decide that a column is text only if `df[col].dtype == object`. In pandas 3, string columns such as `bike_model` (and `date` before parsing) have the `str` dtype, not `object`. So they fall into the "numeric" branch, and `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` turns every value into `NaN`. The functions then flag every row as having an invalid or missing model, or count 12,904 "excess duplicate rows" in a dataset that has none. Nothing fails, so the fix-and-retry loop does not trigger, and the corrupted table is returned as the answer.

## Environment

- Product: AI Data Science Team (business-science/ai-data-science-team) commit 4ffeb7f38178aa250917f29b01355f8b89ba809e, deployed as the repository's Pandas Data Analyst app configuration (`apps/pandas-data-analyst-app/app.py`): `PandasDataAnalyst` (routing preprocessor → `DataWranglingAgent` → optional `DataVisualizationAgent`), `bypass_recommended_steps=True`, `n_samples=100`, `log=False`.
- Data: the repository's `data/bike_sales_data.csv`, pre-loaded as `data_raw` (13,149 rows × 5 columns: `date`, `bike_model`, `price`, `quantity_sold`, `extended_sales`; dates 2021-01-01 to 2024-12-31; no duplicate rows, no missing values).
- Runtime: Python container built from the repository's unpinned `requirements.txt`; the agent's own generated code reported pandas 3.0.6 and numpy 2.5.3 in the same campaign.
- Model: glm-5.3-flash through Zhipu's OpenAI-compatible coding endpoint (`https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4`). The app's `ChatOpenAI` client was routed to it by the harness.
- Setup: in-process LangGraph adapter in Docker, with outbound traffic limited to the model route by an interception proxy. Each case step is one `invoke_agent(user_instructions=<step>, data_raw=df)` call with no shared conversation state. The reply is the graph's summary message plus the first 40 rows of `data_wrangled`, the same table the app displays.
- Test prompts: multi-step scripted test cases. Many of them describe workflows outside this agent's domain; each issue names only the steps where the agent's own behavior is at fault.
- Judge verdict: `issue` for each run. Runs marked "not counted" in an issue were not accepted by the harness because a model call in another step failed (`OpenAIConnectionError`); the steps cited ran normally. The Judge did not receive this LangGraph agent's model turns.
- Evidence source: Captured execution, 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26 UTC. No fresh agent replay on the current release; where stated, recorded generated functions were re-executed offline on the same CSV. The root cause has not been separated between the model and the scaffolding.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the evidence posted with this report (text in the comments below). Use pandas 3.x (the recorded container reported pandas 3.0.6; the replay below used 3.0.3) and the repository's `data/bike_sales_data.csv`.
2. Fastest check, without calling the model: take the final generated function for each case from `evidence/<label>/raw/inputs/<step>/framework.jsonl` (the last `PythonOutputParser` span output), `exec` it, and call `data_wrangler(pd.read_csv("data/bike_sales_data.csv"))`. Count `NaN` in `bike_model` (and `date` for `duplicates`) and read the flag and report columns.
3. Full check: set up the Pandas Data Analyst configuration as listed under Environment, call `invoke_agent(user_instructions=<step text from evidence/<label>/prompt.txt>, data_raw=df)` for the listed step with the recorded model, and read `get_response()` and `get_data_wrangled()`. Code generation is not deterministic, so a new run may produce a function that does not hit this path.

## Expected behavior

Wrangling code should not destroy valid values. A text column that pandas stores as `str` or `string` should be treated as text. If a type conversion turns every value in a column into `NaN`, the function should treat that as a conversion error, not as a data-quality finding about the dataset. The reply should not report missing, invalid or duplicate values that exist only because the agent's own code created them.

## Actual behavior

| Case | What was asked | What the agent did | Why this is a defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| dissent, step 5 | "Preserve a dissent record that documents which source or definition each conflicting total came from and why they disagree." | 13149 rows × 21 cols. `bike_model` is `NaN` in every row; `invalid_bike_model_flag = True` and `missing_bike_model_flag = True` in every row. The code only puts `dtype == object` columns into `cat_cols`; every other column goes to `numeric_cols` → `pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors='coerce')`, and `invalid_{c}_flag` is added when values are lost | The model name, the key of the requested per-model dissent record, is gone from every row. The dataset's 13,149 valid model names are reported as invalid and missing |
| duplicates, step 8 | "Verify that the joined dataset does not contain duplicate rows. If duplicates exist, report the number of duplicate rows and the models involved." | `date` and `bike_model` are `NaN` in every row. `duplicate_report`: "13146 rows are part of duplicate groups (12904 excess duplicate rows); models involved: none." The code: `if joined[col].dtype == object: … else: joined[col] = pd.to_numeric(joined[col], errors='coerce')` | The raw CSV has 0 duplicate rows (`df.duplicated().sum() == 0`). Once the two text columns are erased, the remaining numeric columns repeat, so the agent reports 12,904 duplicates that do not exist, and "models involved: none" |
| capabilities, step 7 | "Negotiate capabilities for the synthetic API contract. Determine which optional features or extensions are supported by the producer and consumer." | `bike_model` is `NaN` in every row, and `has_missing_flag = True` in every row. The code builds `text_cols` only from `object` or `CategoricalDtype` columns; the rest go to `pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce')` | The request is off-domain for this agent, but the returned table still misreports the dataset: every row is flagged as having missing values, and the dataset has none |

Replaying the recorded final function outside the agent, on the same CSV with pandas 3.0.3, reproduces each result exactly: `dissent` gives 13,149 `NaN` in `bike_model` and 13,149 `invalid_bike_model_flag`; `duplicates` gives 13,149 `NaN` in `date` and in `bike_model`, and the same "12904 excess duplicate rows" text; `capabilities` gives 13,149 `NaN` and 13,149 `has_missing_flag`.

Across the 20 runs reviewed with these cases, the agent generated 157 final wrangling functions. Only these three returned a table in which a text column had been emptied. Many other functions also test `dtype == object`, but they convert a column to numeric only when most of its values parse, which avoids the loss. The defect is that nothing stops a function that silently empties a column from being returned as a finished result.

Some parts of these runs are deliberately excluded:

- **Other steps.** `dissent` steps 3–4 and `duplicates` steps 2, 3 and 10 depend on earlier results or on a second dataset (bike model specs) that the harness did not pre-load. Those failures come from the harness or the case and are not reported here.
- **Failed steps.** `duplicates` step 5 and `capabilities` steps 1–2 failed with a model connection error (`OpenAIConnectionError`). They have no output and are not part of this report.

## Evidence

The evidence is posted as text in the comments below; the complete curated files are available on request. They include:

- the full prompts (`prompt.txt`);
- the per-step public responses (`final.txt`, the summary message plus the first 40 table rows);
- the Judge reports;
- per-step framework span logs (`raw/inputs/NNNN/framework.jsonl`);
- per-step results (`raw/inputs/NNNN/result.json`);
- SHA-256 checksums.

The span logs contain the routing decision (`JsonOutputParser`), every generated `data_wrangler` function version (`PythonOutputParser`) and each execution result (`execute_data_wrangler_code`), including fix-retry errors.

This is an in-process LangGraph run with no tool calls. The decisive evidence is the final `PythonOutputParser` span of the listed step (the type-normalization block quoted above) and the returned table in `final.txt`.

## Reproducibility and limitations

Each example is one historical agent run, not a measured reproduction rate. Three of the campaign's generated functions hit this path; how often a fresh run does so depends on the generated code. The offline replay of the recorded functions is deterministic.

The root cause has not been separated between the model (glm-5.3-flash writes `dtype == object` checks), the wrangling prompt (which does not mention pandas 3 string dtypes), and the scaffolding (the retry loop only reacts to exceptions, so a column that is silently emptied is accepted). Upstream pins or supported pandas versions were not checked; the container ran pandas 3.0.6.

The Judge did not receive this agent's model turns. The Judge flagged `duplicates` step 8 for exactly this reason: it "sets date and bike_model to NaN". For `dissent` step 5 and `capabilities` step 7 it flagged the steps for other reasons (a missing dissent record, and an off-domain request); the `NaN` corruption in those two steps was found by reviewing the raw output. The `duplicates` and `capabilities` runs were not counted by the harness because a model call in another step failed.
